In mass spectrometry, the M+1 peak (m/z 95 in this case) compared to the molecular ion peak (M+ at m/z 94) typically represents isotopic contributions, primarily from naturally occurring 13C instead of 12C. 

For small organic molecules like phenol (C6H6O), the M+1 peak intensity relative to the molecular ion peak follows predictable patterns based on natural isotope abundance. The theoretical intensity of the M+1 peak is approximately 6.6% of the molecular ion peak intensity for phenol, due to:

1. The natural abundance of 13C (about 1.1% per carbon atom)
2. The number of carbon atoms in phenol (6 carbons)
3. Small contributions from other isotopes (2H, 17O)
